text.p: Digi International Inc's interim acting chief executive, Jerry Dusa, on Thursday declined to tell shareholders at its annual meeting when the company would return to profitability.

Responding to a shareholder question about when the company would begin showing a profit, he said: "Give me a chance to develop a plan, and I'll come back to you. We will stabilize operations. We're looking at our internal operations and cost structure to return us to profitability."
"We need to launch fewer products and the marketing dollars will make a greater impact," Dusa said. "We had too many products in fiscal year 96, no one of which got enough money."
He said the company would control cost of sales by streamlining its production process. Digi makes data communications hardware and software enabling microcomputers to function as multiuser systems.
"We're going to reduce our manufacturing infrastructure and take some costs out of it," he said without offering any specifics.
